title: Recording drought and the Joe Davis sides
summary: She wasn't in demand and then recorded for Joe Davis with Herman Chittison's trio members including Barksdale.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well you didn't record again for two and a half years.
Yeah. Well, there just wasn't -- I wasn't in demand, number one. And it wasn't that easy to make records. The material, there was a shortage of material.
Of course.

Joe Davis -- this set of things that are coming up now that were made on the Beacon label with Joe Davis -- You know, Joe Davis had a publishing company from way back, and he contacted me. I guess I was pretty desperate to have a hit recording, you know, let's face it. And nothing had happened since 'Loch Lomond.'
Well, in terms of popularity.

That's right.
I certainly wouldn't agree with that statement in terms of quality.

Yeah, yeah, popularity. It wasn't that easy, and as I said before, I came off the road and I went into Le Ruban Bleu. So, I guess I was sort of isolated from the mainstream as when it came to making recordings and... I didn't do any radio then, and I was pretty exclusive. So I didn't get a chance to make any recordings,-- along with the shortage of material and all that. But this Joe Davis outfit and the musicians -- Well Cedric Wallace evidently had access to Joe Davis' publishing, and these are some of the musicians that I had worked with at Le Ruban Bleu. Because Cedric Wallace played with Herman Chittison --
You mentioned him before as part of Herman Chittison Trio.
Right. And Everett

Yeah, who played with Art Tatum.

And so, I had worked with these guys off and on doing little gigs. It might've -- it must've been Cedric -- because Cedric Wallace was the one who approached me about the date.
And these were Joe Davis' songs.

I don't know whether he wrote them --
